title: orchestrate-cred-presets-and-stream-heuristics-across-sdks
author: Priya Kumar
description: Align credential presets, retry/backoff heuristics, and stream cursor semantics across Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs to reduce cross-language developer friction and surface a single migration path for clients. This PR centralizes a small, opinionated set of 'cred profiles' (short-lived, steady, long-haul) exposed consistently across SDKs, standardizes a compact retry DSL used by streaming consumers, and harmonizes stream resume/checkpoint semantics so that SDK consumers can reason about idempotency and reconnection uniformly. Changes include non-breaking API adapters for each SDK, test vectors and interop harness updates, updated docs and migration notes, a version bump for py/ts/go SDK packages, and a small runtime guard in the client that maps legacy credential modes to the new profiles. Motivations: 1) Teams shipping multi-platform clients were repeatedly implementing slightly different backoff curves and token refresh windows, causing subtle 503/timeout differences and noisy telemetry. 2) Stream consumers needed a clearer contract for 'cursor validity' vs 'session leases' to avoid double-processing on reconnect. What changed: introduced three cred profiles with explicit TTL and jittered refresh thresholds, a shared retry preset JSON schema used only for CI/interop, compact stream-checkpoint semantics (peekable cursor with lease_hint), adapters in each SDK that provide both a new ergonomic surface and a thin compatibility layer for the previous API shapes, and bumped public SDK versions (see commits). Testing: cross-language interop harness exercises reconnect + token swap scenarios, unit tests for backoff math, end-to-end smoke tests in the lab. Rollout: feature-flagged on server for two weeks, opt-in toggles in SDKs for beta users, full rollout after telemetry review. Migration notes and examples included in the docs section of the PR.
